title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page sits under the heading 'Métriques canoniques sur surfaces conformes' (previous page). Here X is the Riemann sphere P^1(C), and G = Aut^+(X) = PSL_2(C) is its group of holomorphic automorphisms. Grothendieck lists several kinds of structure on X that turn out to be equivalent: each is a single G-orbit with the same stabiliser.

(a) Two real structures on X 'of opposite type' that are compatible (commuting). The two types are: an antiholomorphic involution with a fixed circle (a reflection) and one without fixed points (an antipodal map). The fixed-point-free involution σ amounts to a choice of spherical metric. Equivalently it amounts to a maximal compact subgroup SO(3) = centraliser of σ, i.e. a point of PSL_2(C)/SO(3) = H^3, which is 3 real parameters. A reflection τ commuting with σ amounts to a great circle for that metric, which is 2 more parameters.

(b) A spherical metric (curvature +1) together with a great circle. This is the same data as (a).

(c) A circle with a compatible toric structure (a circle action), plus a pair of points conjugate with respect to that circle (exchanged by the reflection in it).

(d) A compact torus T ≅ S^1 in G, plus one orbit of T on X minus X^T. The orbits meant are those not reduced to a point, i.e. the T-invariant circles.

(d') A pair of points {z, z'} in X, plus one orbit, on X minus {z, z'}, of the unique compact torus T ⊂ G fixing z and z'.

Equivalence check. Take z = 0 and z' = ∞, so T = {z ↦ e^{iθ} z}. The circle orbit is |z| = r. This data corresponds exactly to:
- the spherical metric 2r|dz|/(r^2 + |z|^2), for which 0 and ∞ are antipodal and |z| = r is the equator;
- the pair of commuting involutions z ↦ -r^2/z̄ (antipodal) and z ↦ r^2/z̄ (reflection).

In every case the stabiliser in PSL_2(C) is O(2): the rotations e^{iθ}z together with z ↦ r^2/z. Every parameter space has real dimension 6 - 1 = 5, matching the counts above.

Purpose: for the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' programme, this gives a canonical rigidification of a sphere with a distinguished circle, or with two marked points (poles). That is exactly the gluing data needed to cut and paste conformal surfaces along circles while keeping canonical metrics. The next page goes on to real structures on tori and abelian varieties: H^1(Γ, E) ≅ H^2(Γ, Z) ≅ Z^g/(1-σ).
errors: No mathematical errors; the equivalences are correct (each is a PSL_2(C)-homogeneous space with stabiliser O(2)).
In (c) the phrase after 'i.e.' is illegible, so the precise formulation cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Equivalence between a spherical metric on P^1 and a fixed-point-free antiholomorphic involution (equivalently a maximal compact SO(3), a point of H^3), and between a great circle and a commuting reflection
ideas.modern_name: Real forms of P^1 / Cartan involutions of PSL_2(C); H^3 as the space of round metrics

ideas.what: Equivalence of (pair of points + circle orbit of the S^1 fixing them) with (spherical metric + great circle)
ideas.modern_name: Homogeneous space PSL_2(C)/O(2); round structure on an annulus or cylinder

ideas.what: Using such rigidified spheres as canonical gluing data for surgery of conformal surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Canonical metrics, pants and annulus decompositions, plumbing coordinates (Strebel, Fenchel–Nielsen-type gluing)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses canonical metrics and surgery on surfaces in broad terms

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary, correct dictionary of equivalent structures on the Riemann sphere. It is useful scaffolding for the surgery programme but classical, with nothing new.

c) second line is illegible after 'i.e.'; the struck-through word and the replacement word cannot be read reliably.
c) last line: 'et paire de points conjugués par ledit [cercle]'.
d): 'orbite de X∖X^T sous T (i.e. orbites non réduites à un point)', confirmed.
